hook_text: Surnames like September, Februarie and Van Java tell a story many South Africans never learnt at school.
clip_script: From 1658, the Dutch East India Company brought enslaved people to the Cape: about sixty-three thousand over a hundred and fifty years. They came from Mozambique and Madagascar, from India and Sri Lanka, from Java, Bali and Timor. They were captured in wars or sold in famines, packed into ships, and sold at auctions in Cape Town. Their owners gave them new names: the month they arrived, or where they came from. September. Van Bengalen. Van Madagascar. Those names are still carried by South Africans today. Their forced labour built the colony.
visual_style: A map of the Indian Ocean with routes converging on the Cape; old handwritten register entries with names appear and then dissolve into modern names on a list.
pacing: Slow and steady, letting the names land.
